llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions match its stated purpose (Windows file search via Voidtools Everything); nothing in the bundle appears to be trying to do unrelated actions, but the skill enables wide filesystem enumeration so review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (instant file search via Voidtools Everything) align with the declared requirement (ev binary) and included assets (CLI and Python API docs). The suggested pip package and MCP optional server are consistent with providing a CLI/API for Everything.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and included docs instruct the agent to perform system-wide file searches and show examples that collect and export paths (including .env files). This is consistent with the stated purpose but enables broad filesystem enumeration and downstream file access; users should be aware of privacy/secret-exposure risk. The SDK docs included mention functions (e.g., Everything_DeleteRunHistory, Everything_Exit) that can change Everything's state — these are part of the SDK docs and are not invoked by the skill's runtime instructions, but they increase the set of available operations if the underlying library is used.

Installing the published pip package is the only install action suggested; verify the package source before installing.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent: it just wraps Voidtools Everything for fast Windows searches. Before installing, confirm you have Everything installed and that the 'ev' binary is present. Review the everyfile pip package contents (on PyPI or source repo) if you plan to pip-install it — the registry only includes docs, not the package itself. Be cautious: the skill performs system-wide file enumeration (examples explicitly show collecting .env files and exporting results), so consider privacy and secret-exposure risk when granting the agent permission to run searches or to access returned paths. If you won't tolerate broad filesystem access, do not enable or invoke this skill. If you enable the optional MCP server, audit its network exposures and only run it if you trust the package and configuration.
